test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 03 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In 2010, considering its outstanding value and vulnerability, UNESCO recognised 'Mudiyettu', an age-old ritual-drama of ______, as an ‘intangible cultural heritage of humanity’.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 2010, considering its outstanding value and vulnerability, **UNESCO** recognised** 'Mudiyettu', **an age-old ritual-drama of Kerala, as an** ‘intangible cultural heritage of humanity’.**
 
• Mudiyettu is a traditional ritual performance deeply rooted in the Goddess Kali cult, primarily practiced by the Marar and Kuruppu communities. The name "Mudiyettu" is derived from the Malayalam words "Mudi" meaning hair and "Ettu" meaning wear.
 
• This performance involves seven key characters: Goddess Bhadrakali, Darika, Lord Shiva, Sage Narada, Dhanavendran, Koyimbadan, and Kooli. Each character adorns vibrantly decorated headgears, costumes, and makeup, enhancing the visual spectacle.
 
• The performance unfolds to the rhythmic beats of traditional percussion instruments. Mudiyettu is traditionally performed in the districts of Ernakulam, Thrissur, Kottayam, and Idukki, which were once part of the old Princely States of Travancore and Cochin in Kerala.
 
• This cultural tradition serves as a vibrant expression of local beliefs and folklore, captivating audiences with its colorful pageantry and spiritual significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kerala,** situated on the Malabar Coast of India, was established on November 1, 1956, through the enactment of the States Reorganisation Act.
 
• This formation amalgamated Malayalam-speaking regions from the former entities of Cochin, Malabar, South Canara, and Travancore. Encompassing an area of 38,863 square kilometers (15,005 square miles), Kerala ranks as the 21st largest state in India by land area.
 
• It shares borders with Karnataka to the north and northeast, Tamil Nadu to the east and south, and the Lakshadweep Sea to the west.
 
• As of the 2011 census, Kerala boasts a population of 33 million, making it the 13th most populous state in India. Administratively, Kerala is divided into 14 districts, with Thiruvananthapuram serving as its capital.
 
• Malayalam stands as the predominant language, serving as both the most commonly spoken tongue and the official language of the state.
